texts.facts: 1. The respondent No.2 being dead, the appeal abates against him. 2. This appeal challenges the legality and correctness of the judgment and order dated 10th October, 2002, rendered in Regular Criminal Case No.34/1996, by the Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Buldhana, acquitting the respondents of the offence punishable under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as, "the PFA Act"). The respondent No.1 and deceased respondent No.2 were charged with an offence of selling and storing under the brand name "WONDER Biscuits" which were adulterated and did not conform to the food standard prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules framed thereunder. The non- conformity was in the nature of presence of acidic extracted fat beyond the prescribed limit. 3. The sample of the biscuits was taken at about 2.00 p.m. of 11.2.1994 from the shop of respondent No.1, situated at village Raipur, District Buldhana. It was stated in the complaint that the sample so taken weighed 1 Kg. and it was divided into three parts, one of which was sent to public analyst, Pune for analysis and report and remaining two samples were handed over in a sealed condition to the Local Health Authority, Buldhana. Needless to say, the sample that was obtained was after payment of its price to the respondent No.1. The report of Public Analysis, Pune was adverse and it stated that the sample that was subjected to analysis was adulterated and did not conform to the Food Standard prescribed under PFA Act and the Rules framed thereunder. Therefore, it was also alleged that these biscuits were manufactured and sold by respondent No.2 to respondent No.1 who in turn stored them for sale and also sold to the complainant. There was no specific allegations made against the respondent Nos.3 and 4. Accordingly, a complaint was filed against all the respondents and they were prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the PFA Act. Not being satisfied with the same, the appellant-State is before this Court in the present appeal. Nobody is present on behalf of respondent Nos.2 & 3.
